summary:
Space Mission Design Simulator

Space exploration involves complex decisions about spacecraft components, resources, and mission requirements. Understanding how these factors affect a space mission can be challenging for beginners and students.
Our solution is an interactive Space Mission Design Simulator that allows users to design their own spacecraft and simulate space missions.
Users can select different spacecraft components, manage budget, mass, and power consumption, validate mission requirements, and launch simulated missions at different difficulty levels.
The platform also includes a NASA Mission Explorer featuring real-world missions such as Mars Perseverance Rover, OSIRIS-REx, Landsat 9, and DART.
Our goal is to make spacecraft design and space exploration more interactive, accessible, and educational.
details:
Space Mission Design Simulator is an interactive platform that lets users design their own spacecraft and simulate space missions. Users select components, manage budget, mass, and power, check mission requirements, and launch simulated missions at different difficulty levels. It also features a NASA Mission Explorer showcasing real missions like Perseverance, OSIRIS-REx, Landsat 9, and DART.

Our goal is to make space exploration easier and more engaging for students through hands-on learning. Users can experiment with different designs, understand resource management, and see how their decisions affect mission success.

We developed the project using Python, Streamlit, JSON, Git, and GitHub. Its creative approach combines spacecraft design, resource management, mission validation, and launch simulation in one interactive experience.

We considered budget, mass, power consumption, mission objectives, and component compatibility while designing the simulator. The values used are simplified for educational purposes, not official NASA specifications.
